subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add native per-token Gateway identities for shared Control UI/team access, and should that design be unified with scoped service-token work such as #92367?
rationale: This changes Gateway auth/config semantics and identity boundaries, so implementation needs an owner decision before an autonomous fix can safely choose token shape, scope vocabulary, and session attribution behavior.

options.title: Sponsor unified scoped-token principals
options.body: Add one Gateway-owned design for token principals that can support both per-user Control UI identity and service-token scope binding while keeping single-token installs compatible.

options.title: Fold this into scoped service tokens
options.body: Close or demote this issue only after #92367 explicitly owns the per-user identity/session behavior, not just route-scoped service credentials.

options.title: Document external frontends only
options.body: Keep core single-token semantics and point teams to trusted-proxy/custom frontend patterns such as the Pinchy-style workaround, accepting that Control UI remains shared-identity only.

recommendation.title: Sponsor unified scoped-token principals
recommendation.body: Add one Gateway-owned design for token principals that can support both per-user Control UI identity and service-token scope binding while keeping single-token installs compatible.

likelyOwner.reason: The local history ties this person most directly to current Gateway auth/config and shared-secret compatibility behavior.
